newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Tel Aviv bourse reopens for stock trading.
newsitem.headline: Tel Aviv bourse reopens for stock trading.

text.p: The Tel Aviv Stock Exchange opened for its main trading session of the 100 most liquid stocks on Wednesday after a strike by Bezeq Israel Telecom workers wreaked havoc with communications on Tuesday.
"Trading has resumed although some telephone disruptions continue," a bourse spokeswoman said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares posted a moderate 0.77 percent increase on its previous closing price in early trading, rising to 295.69.

Mishtanim trading was cancelled on Tuesday when brokerage houses and banks could not get through to the exchange. The morning Meretz call market, bonds, options on the Maof blue chip index and the dollar traded as usual.
A week-long strike over government plans to privatise more of Bezeq has curtailed telephone repair and operator information services.
Employees of state-owned Bezeq returned to their workplaces on Wednesday but refused to comply fully with a labour court order to restore normal telephone services.
Telephone services remained disrupted by 1:30 p.m. (1030 GMT) on Wednesday.
